newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon premier keeps key ministers in new cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Gabon premier keeps key ministers in new cabinet.

text.p: Gabon's Prime Minister Paulin Obame Nguema has unveiled a new cabinet for the Central African country, keeping key ministers but excluding the opposition.
The government, announced by Obame Nguema on national television on Tuesday night, shows continuity in the portfolios of oil, finance and foreign affairs.
The most significant individual change was the departure of Interior Minister Louis-Gaston Mayila, replaced by Antoine Mboumbou Miyakou who was sacked from the same job previously.
Obame Nguema said the outgoing government had been bogged down with purely political issues "and it is about time we relaunched the economy and put emphasis on tackling social problems".

The only member of the opposition coalition named in the new government is Alexandre Sambat, head of the Rally for Democracy and Progress party. Political analysts said his appointment as Youth and Sports Minister might mean he had left the opposition alliance.
President Omar Bongo's party won 100 of parliament's 120 seats in December's legislative election. Bongo has ruled the oil-producing former French colony since 1968.
